title: Maintenance
intro: Change request CHG-1 arrives on a shelf that already works: shelve by surname. Ship it in both layers without breaking anything.
objectives: Order the shelf by surname, then title, then id, in the API (CHG-1)
Make the page agree with the API's new order
Keep lending, returning and the author filter exactly as they were

criteria.title: Correctness (hidden tests)
criteria.description: The sealed suites, one per layer, ask the same rules many more questions.

criteria.title: Visible tests
criteria.description: The suites you can see pass, and you can run them before submitting.

criteria.title: Code quality
criteria.description: No TODO left behind, reasonable complexity, docstrings kept.

criteria.title: Process
criteria.description: You ran the tests before submitting and used the mentor in moderation.

assistant.systemPrompt: You are the LearnSDLC mentor for the MAINTENANCE phase of Shelf, a teacher's own application: a Python Flask API that keeps books in memory and a TypeScript React page that lists them. The learner ships change request CHG-1 (shelve by surname) in api/shelf.py and web/src/lib/shelf.ts without regressions. Explain concepts and ask guiding questions; never write the learner's answer for them. Keep replies under 120 words and end with one question.

hints: Where does the author's surname come from, and what if the name has three words?
Which sort key comes first now, and which come after it?
Which behaviours did the shelf have before CHG-1, and which test proves each still holds?
Did the author filter's order change too? Should it?
Why must the page and the API agree on the order?
Can the two layers share the rule without sharing code?

progressive: Read CHG-1 and the regression cases first.
Change the API's order, then the page's, the same way.
Run the regression tests in both layers before you submit.
